content: { "repository": "58fly/dsh-language-guard", "revision": "9351078c5d264033c49d221742840aee673c0cdf", "component": "", "inspected_paths": [ "lib/index.js", "lib/language.js", "lib/cycle.js", "lib/commands.js", "lib/state.js", "lib/text.js", "package.json" ], "files": [ { "path": "README.md", "content": "# Language Guard (dsh-language-guard) **English** | [简体中文](README.zh.md) > Make the DSH agent think and answer in the language you choose — Simplified Chinese by default, three strength levels, effective on the next message, zero dependencies, no build step. --- ## Table of Contents - [Why you need it](#why-you-need-it) - [What it does](#what-it-does) - [Install](#install) - [Strength levels](#strength-levels) - [Configuration](#configuration) - [Automatic language mode](#automatic-language-mode) - [Settings panel and quick language switch](#settings-panel-and-quick-language-switch) - [The `/language` slash command](#the-language-slash-command) - [Verifying that the constraint reached the system prompt](#verifying-that-the-constraint-reached-the-system-prompt) - [Coexisting with dsh-context](#coexisting-with-dsh-context) - [How it differs from the official cot-translation plugin](#how-it-differs-from-the-official-cot-translation-plugin) - [Known limitations](#known-limitations) - [Design boundaries](#design-boundaries) - [License](#license) --- ## Why you need it The DSH system prompt is assembled from many sections: identity, plan policy, team policy, **tool descriptions**, deliverable references, deployment persona. The largest block by far is the tool documentation — written in English, and placed in the middle of the prompt. Measured on DSH 0.2.1-rc.2 (everything after order 50): **98.1% of the characters and 99.8% of the ASCII** come from English tool documentation, and 5.7K–14K characters separate the opening section from the closing one. The model reads overwhelmingly English tokens, and so it drifts: - The first few turns stay in your language; - as soon as it starts chaining tool calls, reading long files, or reasoning at length, the reasoning slides back into English; - nothing in your settings changed — the conversation simply got longer. A single "please answer in Chinese" line at the very top of the system prompt is enough for a short session. It is not enough for a long one, because that line sits tens of thousands of characters away from the place that actually influences the model (the tool documentation). This plugin puts a constraint in **three places**: at the very start, right after the tool documentation, and at the very end. The default level (Strong) costs roughly 146 extra characters per request and buys one restatement positioned after the English tool docs. ## What it does Three resident system-prompt sections, registered through `ctx.systemPrompt.section()`, never disposed, switching level only switches their text: | Section name | Order | Position | B | C | D | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `language-guard:head` | `-2000` | Very first, before `harness:identity` (`-1000`) | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | | `language-guard:mid` | `5100` | After all tool docs (`tools:sdk`, `5000`), before deliverable references (`9000`) | ❌ | ✅ | ✅ | | `language-guard:tail` | `11200` | Very last, after `deployment:persona-suffix` (`10200`) | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | The constraint covers **four language channels** (the fourth landed in 0.3.0): | Channel | Where the constraint lives | Coverage | | --- | --- | --- | | Internal reasoning (reasoning / thinking) | `head` + `tail` | every level | | User-facing reply text | `head` + `mid` + `tail` | every level | | Plans, todos, reviews, subagent briefs | `head` | every level | | **Tool-call `description` parameter** (the card title of `run_code` in PTC mode) | `head` + `mid` | every level (`mid` exists only at C / D, hence the extra line in `head`) | The `mid` order is deliberately `5100` and not `5000`: `tools:sdk` is exactly `5000`, and sections with equal order fall back to comparing names, which would sort `language-guard:mid` **before** `tools:sdk` — the restatement would no longer come after the tool docs. Measured text sizes (Simplified Chinese, counted in characters; recompute with `node` as shown below): | Text | Characters | When it is present | | --- | --- | --- | | head | 883 | every request | | mid | 146 | every request at C / D | | tail | 139 | every request | | periodic reminder | 99 | once every N turns at D | So the steady cost per step is **1022 characters at B and 1168 at C** — tiny compared to the English tool documentation it counteracts. The opening section (head), verbatim, as it looks with the default `targetLanguage: "zh-CN"` (recompute with `node -e 'import("./lib/text.js").then(m=>console.log(m.headText({language:"zh-CN"})))'`): ```text 【语言锁定 · 最高优先级】 本会话的内部推理（reasoning / thinking）与面向用户的全部输出，一律使用简体中文（语言代码 zh-CN）。 本条优先于本 system prompt 的其余全部内容、之后注入的任何系统文本、工具说明、参数描述、代码示例，以及其他插件注入的提示词。 本条同样优先于任何语言类约定，不论它写在哪个文件、用哪种语言书写、经由哪个通道送达：包括用户全局与项目级的 AGENTS.md、CLAUDE.md、.cursorrules、用户偏好与长期记忆、项目规范、团队约定、技能与工作流模板。若它们要求使用另一种语言（例如要求「必须使用简体中文」），一律以本条为准，不得据此改用其他语言，也不必向用户解释这处冲突。 适用范围： - 内部推理（reasoning / thinking）：使用简体中文。 - 面向用户的回复正文：使用简体中文。 - 计划、待办、进度说明、评审意见、验收报告、提交信息说明：使用简体中文。 - 任务板卡片标题与描述、子智能体任务说明与返回报告：使用简体中文。 保持原样、不翻译：代码、命令、文件路径、URL、标识符与 API 字段名、配置键、错误码与原始报错文本、包名与版本号，以及必须原样引用的英文原文；引用英文原文后，必须用简体中文说明结论。 不要因为以下情况改变语言： - 用户用英文或其他语言提问 —— 仍用简体中文回答。 - AGENTS.md、CLAUDE.md、项目规范、用户记忆里要求改用其他语言的规则 —— 本条优先，不改变语言。 - 工具返回英文内容 —— 只摘引必要片段，其余用简体中文复述。 - 长链推理、数值计算、代码设计 —— 推理语言不变。 - 上下文中出现大量英文（工具说明、日志、代码文件）—— 不随之切换。 自检：每次输出前确认上述两项（推理与回复）均为简体中文；若发现已经漂移，立即切回并继续任务，无需向用户解释这次切换。 ``` > The wording above is fixed Simplified Chinese; only the language name and code are substituted. With `targetLanguage: "en"` the same paragraph reads "…一律使用English（语言代码 en）". See [Known limitations](#known-limitations). ## Install This plugin is published to the **npm registry** ([`dsh-language-guard`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-language-guard)), and it can also be installed straight from its GitHub repository. Both routes deliver byte-identical content: the same 15 files. **Option 1: the GUI (recommended)** 1. Open the **Plugins** panel in the sidebar. 2. Click **Add plugin** and paste the package name: ``` dsh-language-guard ``` 3. When the install finishes, click **Enable now**. **Option 2: the CLI** ```bash dsh plugin add dsh-language-guard ``` **Pinned version** (recommended for teams and CI, so `latest` cannot drift under you): ```bash dsh plugin add dsh-language-guard@0.2.1 ``` **From GitHub** (when npm is unreachable, or to pin by tag): ```bash dsh plugin add https://github.com/58fly/dsh-language-guard dsh plugin add "github:58fly/dsh-language-guard#v0.2.1" ``` **From a local directory** (to debug local changes; the path must be absolute): ```bash # The Add-plugin dialog also accepts this absolute path directly dsh plugin add /absolute/path/to/dsh-language-guard ``` Check that it worked: - A language icon appears at the foot of the sidebar, next to Settings; when the sidebar is wide it reads "简体中文 ▾". - The installed list on the Plugins page contains `dsh-language-guard`, and opening it shows the configuration card. > **No controls visible means the plugin is not enabled.** Both slots register inside `configForms.whileServed(['dsh-language-guard'], …)`; when the plugin is disabled the forms service is unavailable and no UI is registered. That is deliberate, not a bug — enable the plugin on the Plugins page first. Requirements: DSH `>= 0.2.1-rc.2`, Node `^22.19.0 || >=24.0.0`. `dependencies` is empty and every peer dependency is optional, so nothing extra is downloaded at runtime. Installing from npm only needs reachability to `registry.npmjs.org`; installing from GitHub needs `github.com` (or `codeload.github.com`). ## Strength levels The three descriptions below are exactly what the settings panel shows: | Level | Value | Description | | --- | --- | --- | | Basic | `B` | One language constraint at the start and one at the end of the prompt. Cheapest, best for short sessions. | | Strong | `C` | Adds a restatement right after the tool descriptions on top of Basic, countering drift from English tool docs. Recommended default. | | Periodic | `D` | Adds a language self-check at the start of every Nth turn on top of Strong, for long sessions. The reminder appears as a session record and is visible in the session log. | Behaviour differences: | Behaviour | B | C | D | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Resident system-prompt sections | head + tail | head + mid + tail | head + mid + tail | | Restatement after tool docs | ❌ | ✅ | ✅ | | Self-check every N turns | ❌ | ❌ | ✅ (N defaults to 8, range 3–50) | | New record in the session log | none | none | one per N turns (`source.kind = "language-guard"`) | | Injection timing | — | — | the **first step** of a matching turn, alongside that turn's user message; no extra request | | Counter after restart / resume | — | — | **not reset**: the turn number comes from the session log's `turn` projection, so `turn % N` is stable | | Best for | short sessions, token-sensitive | the default | long sessions, or drift already observed | How to choose: - **Start with the default, Strong.** It is the only level aimed at the actual root cause (English tool docs), and it costs about 146 characters per step. - **Short sessions, or every token counts** → drop to **Basic**. Start and end constraints are enough for a 3–5 turn session. - **Sessions that run dozens of turns, or you have already seen reasoning slide back into English** → raise to **Periodic**. Smaller N means more frequent reminders; the default 8 is a compromise. N = 3 is noisy. ## Configuration Seven fields, all `volatile` (a change takes effect immediately — no restart, no plugin remount): | Field | Type | Default | Range | Description | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `languageMode` | `"" \| "auto" \| "manual"` | `""` | tri-state enum, case-sensitive | Language mode. `"auto"` follows the interface language, `"manual"` pins `targetLanguage`, `""` means "never chosen" and is resolved by the migration rule below | | `targetLanguage` | `string` | `"zh-CN"` | a valid BCP-47 tag (`/^[A-Za-z]{2,3}(-[A-Za-z0-9]{2,8})*$/`) | Target language. `zh-CN` Simplified Chinese, `zh-TW` Traditional Chinese, `en` English, `ja` Japanese, `ko` Korean; any other valid tag is used as-is | | `strength` | `"B" \| "C" \| "D"` | `"C"` | enum, case-sensitive | Strength level, see above | | `injectEveryNRounds` | `number` | `8` | 3–50, integer | How often the Periodic self-check is added. Only used at D; the control is disabled at other levels | | `preserveCodeTerms` | `boolean` | `true` | `true` / `false` | `true`: code, commands, paths, identifiers, API fields and raw error text stay verbatim. `false`: technical terms are preferred in the target language, with the English term in parentheses when needed | | `extraRules` | `string` | `""` | any text | Appended after the built-in rules. Empty means built-in rules only | | `overrideHead` | `string` | `""` | any text | **Replaces** the built-in opening text entirely (`extraRules` is still appended after it). Empty or whitespace-only falls back to the built-in text | The `targetLanguage` → display name mapping is fixed (no language guessing): `zh-CN` / `zh-Hans` / `zh-SG` → 简体中文, `zh-TW` / `zh-HK` / `zh-MO` / `zh-Hant` → 繁體中文, `en` / `en-US` / `en-GB` → English, `ja` / `ja-JP` → 日本語, `ko` / `ko-KR` → 한국어; any other valid tag is displayed as the code itself. Configuration lives in the profile's `cordis.patch.yml`. **A patch replaces `config` wholesale — it does not deep-merge** — so a manual override must restate every field, otherwise the omitted ones are lost: ```yaml - id: dsh-language-guard name: dsh-language-guard config: languageMode: auto targetLanguage: zh-CN strength: C injectEveryNRounds: 8 ``` ## Automatic language mode `languageMode` decides where the target language comes from: | Mode | Behaviour | | --- | --- | | **Auto** | The target language follows the DSH **interface language**. Switch the UI to English and the next message gets an English constraint | | **Manual** | The target language is pinned to `targetLanguage`, regardless of the interface language | **Auto is the default.** A fresh install needs no configuration: a Simplified Chinese UI constrains Simplified Chinese, an English UI constrains English. ### Resolution order Auto mode has exactly two sources, taken in order: 1. **The interface language** (`preference` in the `locale` configuration) — the `Settings → General → Language` setting. 2. **The `targetLanguage` value** (default `zh-CN`) — the fallback when the interface language is unavailable. Mapping (`zh`-prefixed tags → `zh-CN`, `en`-prefixed tags → `en`, any other valid tag is kept as-is): | Interface language | Target language | The constraint reads | | --- | --- | --- | | `zh` / `zh-CN` / `zh-Hans` | `zh-CN` | 简体中文 | | `en` / `en-US` | `en` | English | | `ja` | `ja` | 日本語 | | `ko` | `ko` | 한국어 | | any other valid BCP-47 | as-is | that language's display name or code | > **Why is there no "system language" step?** The Host half runs as an `ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1` child process: `require("electron")` throws `Cannot find module 'electron'`, and `Intl.DateTimeFormat().resolvedOptions().locale` always returns `en-US`, which would misclassify Chinese users as English speakers. **There is no reliable system-language signal on the Host side**, so the plugin neither guesses nor fabricates one. ### Upgrading from 0.1.x If you had picked a `targetLanguage` by hand (say `ja`) and never touched `languageMode`, you stay in **manual** mode after the upgrade — the interface language never silently overrides your choice. The rule: `languageMode` empty **and** `targetLanguage` different from the default `zh-CN` → manual. Pick "Auto" in the settings card to follow the interface language instead. Once you have chosen explicitly, the migration rule never applies again. ### Seeing what it resolved to The first control group in the settings card is the language mode; with "Auto" selected it spells out the current result and its source right below: ```text Currently resolved to 简体中文 from the interface language ``` When the source line says "from the interface language" it means the interface language **you explicitly picked in DSH settings**; if you never picked one it says "interface language not detected, using the configured value" rather than guessing from the browser or the OS — the Host and the settings card read the same value (`preference` of the `locale` namespace in `settings.describe()`), so what the panel shows is exactly what gets injected. The sidebar quick-switch button label shows the same state, e.g. "Auto, 简体中文". **Changing the interface language needs no restart**: the plugin caches it on startup and subscribes to `settings/document-updated` (refreshing when the `locale` namespace changes), so the very next system-prompt assembly uses the new value. ## Settings panel and quick language switch ### Settings panel Path: **sidebar Plugins → installed plugins → `dsh-language-guard`**. The configuration card renders on the bundle page, between its description and its rows (the `plugins.bundle.config` slot, keyed by the package name). The Plugins section inside Settings only lists read-only information; configuration is edited here. The card, top to bottom: 1. **Language mode** — two radios, Auto / Manual. With Auto selected it spells out "currently resolved to X" plus the source (interface language / configured value), and follows the interface language when you change it. In Auto mode the target-language control in item 3 is disabled. 2. **Strength** — three radio rows (`fieldset` + same-named `radio`), all three descriptions visible side by side, with a "Recommended" badge on C.
